paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of context masking on case tasks groupby by language family. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, for six different multilingual BERT model variants: mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂, as indicated in the legend. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to 30 and represents the magnitude of the masking effect, with error bars denoting the standard deviation for each measurement. The horizontal axis categorizes languages into families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. For most language families, the models show varying degrees of effect, with IE-Indic exhibiting the highest values across several models—particularly mBERT-R₂ (~20), mBERT-B₂ (~24), and XLM-B₂ (~21)—while Isolate and Uralic generally show near-zero effects across all models. The bars are grouped by language family, with each group containing six colored bars corresponding to the models, arranged consistently from left to right as per the legend. Notably, mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ tend to show higher effects in IE-Indic, IE-Slavic, and Semitic families, while mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ often show moderate effects in IE-Germanic and IE-Slavic. The chart does not sort the language families by effect size, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and error bars.
